title: Materials: float/sink, hard/soft
examples: Teacher, can we test if this leaf will float?
Is wood always hard, or can it be soft too?
How do we know if something will sink before we drop it?

explain.say: Today we are going to learn about materials. We will look at how things feel and how they behave in water.
First, we can describe materials by how they feel. Some things are very hard, like a rock. Other things are soft, like cotton wool.

draw.text: Hard things feel strong. Soft things feel gentle.

explain.say: Next, we can test if things float or sink in water. If it floats, it stays on top. If it sinks, it goes to the bottom.

draw.text: Float stays up. Sink goes down.

explain.say: We can predict what will happen next. If it is light and smooth, we can guess it will float. If it is heavy and bumpy, we might guess it will sink.

faq.q: How do I know if something is hard or soft?
faq.a: You can gently try to press it or feel its texture. Hard things do not change shape easily, while soft things do.
asks: What is the difference between hard and soft?
Can I test if something is soft?

faq.q: If something floats, does it mean it is light?
faq.a: Floating usually means it is less dense than water, but some heavy things can also float. It is not always the case.
asks: Is floating the same as being light?
Why do some heavy things float?

faq.q: Can I predict if something will sink?
faq.a: You can look at its shape and how much space it takes up. Things that are very heavy for their size often sink.
asks: How can I guess if something sinks?

faq.a: No, wood can be very hard, like oak. But some types of wood can feel quite soft too.

faq.q: What is the best way to test if something sinks?
faq.a: The best way is to carefully place it in a container of water and watch what happens. This is a simple test.
asks: Should I use water to test?

facts: Rocks are usually described as hard materials.
Cotton wool is an example of a soft material.
Objects that float stay on the surface of the water.
Predicting means guessing what will happen next.

quiz.say: Which material is usually described as soft?
quiz.why: Cotton wool feels very gentle and easily squished, which describes soft.

wrong.1: Rocks are usually hard because they are solid and tough.
wrong.2: Wood can be hard, but cotton wool is the best example of soft.
wrong.3: Plastic can be hard or soft, but cotton wool is the clearest example of soft.

quiz.say: If an object sinks, what does that mean?
quiz.why: Sinking means the object is heavier than the water it pushes out of the way.

wrong.0: Floating away suggests it is carried by the water, not necessarily sinking.
wrong.1: Sinking describes the final resting place, not just the speed.

quiz.say: Which item do you predict will float?
quiz.why: Leaves are often light and have a surface that allows them to float on water.

wrong.0: Keys are made of metal and are usually heavy enough to sink.
wrong.2: Stones are usually very heavy and will sink to the bottom.
wrong.3: While feathers are light, a small feather might sink if it gets wet enough.
